report: I facilitated three sisters (A, B, and C) after their father's death, keeping a numbered list of concerns that all three could see. The list as it stands: 1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount"; she wants her fair share. 2. B could use money from the estate, possibly to start a dance studio. 3. All three agreed to review the will and estate documents and get an independent market appraisal. 4. No one knows who the executor is or where the will is held; this must be found out first. Next steps agreed: C will check their father's papers at home for a lawyer's details, B will check the bank or other records, and A will contact the lawyer once identified. Whoever finds the details will report back, and the will review and appraisal can then begin. No price or sale terms have been agreed, and no one committed to any sale terms. I did not make legal decisions or move money.
